one_liner: Senior manager of PBGC's federal contracting team, leading contract specialists and advising executives on complex acquisitions worth over $300 million.
fit_summary: This GS-15 role requires a year of GS-14-equivalent experience leading procurement professionals, at least 4 years in contracting, 24 semester hours in business-related fields, and mandatory 1102 training. Daniel's known background is emergency-management consulting at IEM plus policy knowledge and people skills, not hands-on contract formation, so you would almost certainly not meet minimum qualifications. Under direct hire, qualifications are the only screen.
eligibility: Open to the public under Direct Hire Authority; veterans' preference does not apply, and no federal status is needed.

One year of specialized experience at or equivalent to GS-14 leading procurement professionals and overseeing complex pre-award and contract formation work (acquisition strategy, source selection, cost/price analysis, negotiations, awards).
At least 4 years of contracting or related experience plus completion of mandatory training for GS-13+ contracting positions.

A bachelor's degree including or supplemented by at least 24 semester hours in accounting, business, finance, law, contracts, purchasing, economics, industrial management, marketing, quantitative methods, or organization and management.
Purchase card, COR-only, small business office, or simplified-acquisition-only experience does not qualify. All requirements must be met by the closing date.
strategy: Be honest about whether your IEM work included leading federal contract pre-award activity, such as writing proposals against RFPs, pricing, or negotiating. Supporting a contractor's bids is not the same as government-side contract formation, so do not overstate it.

If you lack 4+ years of contracting and supervisory experience at the GS-14 level, skip this posting. Target entry-level GS-1102 contract specialist trainee or Acquisition Career intern roles (GS-5/7/9) instead, which build toward jobs like this.

Separately pursue roles that match your strengths: FEMA and state VDEM emergency-management or program specialist positions, legislative or constituent-services staff jobs, and Prince William County or City of Manassas public-facing roles.

If you apply anyway, check that your degree coursework totals 24 semester hours in the listed fields and upload transcripts. On a two-page resume, list hours per week, dates, and contract dollar values for each relevant job.
Apply on the day the posting opens (October 14, 2026), because it closes after the first 100 applications.
resume_bullets: Supported [proposal/contract] activities for [number] government emergency-management engagements valued at [$ amount], including [pricing inputs/compliance reviews/requirement analysis] ([hours]/week, [dates]).
Coordinated with [federal/state/local] client stakeholders to clarify [scope of work/deliverables] for [program name], resolving [issue] to keep [contract/task order] on schedule.
Led or mentored [number] team members on [task], setting priorities and reviewing work quality for [client/project].
interview_questions: Describe how you developed an acquisition strategy and selected a contract type for a complex, high-dollar requirement.
Walk us through a source selection or cost/price analysis you oversaw, and the negotiation outcome.
How do you manage the performance of contract specialists and resolve conflicts on a team?
Tell us about a time you persuaded senior stakeholders to accept a novel acquisition approach.
watch_outs: The posting may close early after 100 applications, so the 3-week window could shrink to days.
The degree and 24-semester-hour education requirement is strict; a waiver is solely at the senior procurement executive's discretion and unlikely for an outside applicant.
Contractor-side consulting experience generally does not count as government-side contract formation and supervision at the GS-14 level.
The position is Washington, DC based with telework but not remote, so expect a commute from Manassas.
